source.title_on_document: Story Forge: A Card-Based Framework for AI-Assisted Interactive Storytelling

supplement.where: Appendix A. Narrative Output Cases, pp. 31-32 of this PDF (referred to on p. 21, Section 4.5)
supplement.holds: Two screenshots of example AI-generated story steps. No statistics. No separate online supplement is mentioned; the Data Availability Statement (p. 31) says the data are on University of Plymouth's OneDrive, with no link.

paper_design_summary: Thirty university students were randomly divided into a control group that wrote interactive stories with the web-based AI Story Writer (Squibler) and an experimental group that used Story Forge, a card-based interface that sends user-selected story cards to the Doubao language model. Each arm ran as three sessions of five participants, 35 minutes each. Outcomes are interaction-log metrics (writing time, number of decisions, path branches, choice coverage, causal-relationship strength, repeat visits, new-path discovery) and self-reported SUS, Creativity Support Index, and User Participation Index scores; no creativity or diversity rating of the stories is reported.

studies.label: Story Forge vs AI Story Writer, interactive story writing (30 students)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Writing tool: Story Forge card-based AI interface (experimental) vs web-based AI Story Writer by Squibler (control)
assignment.quote: We enrolled 30 university students (15 males, 15 females) with expertise in AI tools and story creation (M = 2.53, SD = 0.95) into a study. Participants were randomly divided into a control group and an experimental group.

arms.name: Story Forge (experimental)
arms.description: Card-based adaptive interface: users drag character, event/plot, emotion, and scene cards into story-stage slots; the Doubao LLM (v3.5, ByteDance) generates branching story text from the card combination. Three groups of five, 35 min sessions after 10 min training.

arms.name: AI Story Writer (control)
arms.description: Web-based Squibler AI Story Generator (genre menu, creativity slider, story-plot prompt box); predetermined story theme and creation duration. Three groups of five, 35 min sessions after 10 min training.

participants.exclusions: None reported. Per-arm n is not printed in any results table. Arm sizes of 15 come from three groups of five per arm (p. 19, p. 20) and from 15 story drafts per arm (p. 21). The paper states 'This study included a sample of 30 participants' (p. 29).
participants.who: University students (15 male, 15 female) with expertise in AI tools and story creation; none had prior exposure to the narrative writing system. Section 5.6 says occupational backgrounds were 70% students with mean writing experience 15.4 years, which conflicts with 'university students' elsewhere.
participants.country: not_stated (authors at University of Plymouth, UK; funding from the Chinese Government Scholarship)
participants.quote: To accommodate computer and platform constraints, each group was capped at five participants, which resulted in three control groups and three experimental groups with gender balance.
participants.locator: p. 19, Section 4.3; p. 20, Section 4.3; p. 21, Section 4.5; p. 29, Section 5.6

ai_tool.name_model: Treatment: Story Forge built on Doubao AI LLM (Version 3.5, ByteDance) via Unity front end and Node.js back end. Control: Squibler AI Story Writer (web tool; model not stated).
ai_tool.how_used: In Story Forge, users select and arrange story-element cards (character, event, emotion, scene) in slots; the AI turns the card combination into structured prompts and generates branching story text and choices. In the control, users entered a story plot prompt with genre and creativity settings and the tool generated a story. Both arms had generative AI throughout.

task.description: Interactive branching story creation: story creation, plot expansion, and branching plot development on a predetermined story theme.
task.duration: 35 min session per group, after a 10 min training session; individual interviews averaged 25 min afterwards (pp. 20-21)

outcomes.name: Creativity Support Index (CSI)
outcomes.question: none

company_involvement.description: No company authors or funding. Story Forge calls ByteDance's Doubao LLM API and the control uses Squibler's commercial web tool; funding is the Chinese Government Scholarship, grant 202308060116.

data_and_code.data_url: Not given; 'The data can be found at University of Plymouth's OneDrive.' (p. 31)

eligibility.reason: Individuals were randomly divided between two AI tools (Story Forge vs AI Story Writer), an ai_design contrast, so criterion 1 is met. Only 30 participants were enrolled (p. 19), below 50. No outcome rates the creativity, novelty, or cross-person diversity of the stories: the outcomes are interaction logs and self-reported SUS/CSI/UPI, and the authors state the evaluation lacks 'third-party objective assessment of the quality of the content that is produced' (p. 29). The two trained raters mentioned on p. 21 rated collaboration levels, and no results from them are reported; planned output metrics (word count, diversity of story elements, p. 21) are not reported.

one_line_finding: With 30 students randomly split between Story Forge and a web AI story tool, Story Forge users reported higher Creativity Support Index scores (3.9 vs 3.5, t = 2.48, p = 0.041, d = 0.53, FDR-corrected p = 0.061; p. 24 Table 9, p. 25) and logged more decisions and branches, but no creativity rating of the stories is reported.
open_questions: Section 4.3 (p. 19) says the same 30 students 'were selected for the pilot study to validate the fundamental features of the system'; it is unclear whether the pilot and the comparative experiment are the same sessions.
Per-arm analyzed n is never printed; 15 per arm is implied by three groups of five per arm and by 15 story drafts per arm.

Reported t and p values are internally inconsistent for about 28 df (e.g., t = 5.41 with p = 0.015, t = 5.58 with p = 0.012, Tables 6-7), and the CSI/UPI scale range is given as 7-point (pp. 18, 21) and as 1-5 (Table 4).
Population description conflicts: 'university students' (p. 19) vs '70% students' with mean writing experience 15.4 years (p. 29).
notes: Both arms use generative AI, so the contrast is ai_design with Story Forge as the tested configuration and Squibler AI Story Writer as the control. All ten quantitative outcomes in Tables 6-9 are listed with question 'none' because none scores the creativity or diversity of the written stories; exploration path complexity and causal relationship strength are computed on the story structure but measure branching and logical coherence. Qualitative interview outcomes (Table 5, Section 5.3) are not listed. The paper notes it did not examine generative-AI homogenization (p. 29).
